reason: E1 directly supports grain refinement, defect reduction, and hardness increase for a RHEA under ultrasonic-assisted laser cladding, though on a different substrate. E2 shows laser cladding can improve wear resistance of coatings on TC4, but uses a different alloy system and no ultrasonic vibration, so the combined premise of ultrasonic-assisted RHEA on TC4 is only partly supported.
premises: Ultrasonic vibration during laser cladding refines grain structure from columnar to equiaxed in RHEA coatings
Ultrasonic vibration reduces pores and cracks in laser-clad RHEA coatings
Ultrasonic vibration increases microhardness of RHEA coatings on a substrate
Laser cladding can deposit multi-principal alloy coatings on TC4 with improved wear resistance
